messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: p99 latency spike and elevated 504s on /v1/generate — started ~2m ago. Affected region: us-west-2. Auto-scaling did not absorb the load. tags: deploy-rollout-2026-03-15 :rotating_light:
Eve (on-call): seeing this in dashboards. p95 ~1200ms -> 1800ms, p99 jumping to 6.2s. 504s increasing from ~0.05% to 3.8%. Is this the canary?
Sam (backend): can confirm, latest canary (deploy/2026-03-15-09:02) rolled at 09:02 UTC. Traffic split 10%. Logs show a raft of `kv_cache` misses and `http: timeout` to runtime proxy. Posting quick log sample:
```
[09:07:12] upstream timeout id=abc123 route=/v1/generate latency=6200ms code=504 model=redwood-xl-qkv
[09:07:13] kv_cache_miss shard=5 key=ctx_... backend=runtime-3
[09:07:14] error: rpc deadline exceeded
```
Jordan (runtime): that stack looks like the new matrix-attn kernel path hitting a hotspot with long-tail token attention. Could be memory thrash on certain context lengths. I'm checking node heat and GC/pinned memory.
Alex (sre): immediate mitigations: 1) reduce canary to 0% (full rollback of canary) 2) enable automatic fallback to m-compat on gateway 3) increase connection keepalive and short-circuit slow RPCs. Thoughts?
Sam (backend): +1 to rollback. We have a fast rollback script: `./deploy/rollback.sh canary-2026-03-15-0902` — will start unless there's a compelling reason to patch live.
Eve (on-call): customer-impact estimate? Priya (cs) map?
Priya (cs): CS: tickets trending from two enterprise customers in us-west; latency alerts from internal SLO monitors; revenue-impact unknown but we should prepare an outbound if >10% of requests affected for >15m. Current error volume ~2.5% of total requests to /v1/generate.
DeployBot: Rollback triggered by Alex (sre) for canary-2026-03-15-0902 — start 09:09:02 UTC. ETA 90s. :rocket:
Eve (on-call): rolling back now. Sam, can you also flip runtime routing to fallback-compat as a precaution? Jordan, check node thrash and whether we need to cordon any hosts.
Sam (backend): routing update pushed: `gateway.routes.update('/v1/generate', fallback_model='redwood-xl-mcompat')` — now routing 100% of canary path to mcompat variant for 10s window to observe.
Jordan (runtime): I'm seeing two nodes with sustained 95th CPU and rising memory pressure: runtime-3 and runtime-7. Cordoning runtime-3 for investigation.
Eve (on-call): cordoned runtime-3 (marked draining). Monitoring effect on p99.
[~30s later]
Alex (sre): rollback completed @09:10:35 UTC according to DeployBot. DeployBot: Rollback finished for canary-2026-03-15-0902 — status: success.
DeployBot: Traffic switch complete. Rolling metrics check for next 5m.
Sam (backend): initial numbers: error rate dropped from 3.8% -> 0.12% within 30s of rollback and routing change. p99 down to 450ms.
Eve (on-call): good signal. Keeping pager open for 15m to watch for recurrences. Priya, can you draft a short customer note I can share with PMs? We haven't confirmed root cause yet.
Priya (cs): Drafting: "We observed elevated latency and a small number of 504 errors after a canary deploy. We rolled back the canary; service normalized. We're investigating and will follow up with details and mitigation." Will post in #customer-updates if approved.
Jordan (runtime): dug into runtime logs: the new kernel path added a hot lock under heavy prefix cache misses. On certain long contexts (>1024 tokens) the KV lookup caused blocking RPCs; combined with small host memory resulted in degraded tail latency. I'll capture traces and open an issue: `runtime#4382`.
Sam (backend): also noticed increased contention on the router's connection pool — will add circuit-breakers and length-based routing heuristic to keep long-context requests on dedicated pool.
Alex (sre): Post-incident immediate action items:
- [ ] revert canary (done)
- [ ] add temporary fallback routing for long contexts (Sam)
- [ ] cordon/inspect runtime-3,7 (Jordan)
- [ ] add emergency rate limit for anonymous traffic to reduce blast radius (Eve)
- [ ] customer comms draft and send (Priya/Alex)
Eve (on-call): handing off to Jordan for deep-dive. If anything flares, ping me @eve. Oncall shift ends in 40m.
Jordan (runtime): taking over for postmortem. I'll capture heapdumps, perf traces, and link to `runtime#4382`. Planning a recreate in staging with synthetic long-context load.
Priya (cs): Customer note posted to #customer-updates. Slack snippets: "We experienced a short latency spike and elevated 504s tied to a canary deploy. We rolled back the canary and traffic is healthy. We will follow up with a technical update."
Alex (sre): tagging for follow-up: owners: Sam (backend), Jordan (runtime), Alex (sre). Please add timelines for fixes in the follow-up thread.
Eve (on-call): closing immediate pager if metrics stable for 15m. Current window: p99 = 420ms, error rate = 0.08%. Will update in 15m. :white_check_mark:
Jordan (runtime): opening notes and next steps in ops board: https://redwood.internal/ops/runtime/4382 — will attach traces and initial hypothesis.
Sam (backend): I'll schedule a small config tweak to the gateway to avoid routing long-context to the new kernel until we've validated.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 09:25 UTC — metrics stable, no active customer escalations. Pager: resolved -> monitoring.
Eve (on-call): logging this as a P1->P2 transition and will add to postmortem queue. Good catch everyone. :clap:
